--- title: "Movement models" author: "Richard Chandler" date: "2025-11-18" format: revealjs: theme: default embed-resources: false toc: true toc-depth: 2 toc-title: Outline code-fold: false echo: true description: | Random walks --- # Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## Movement models ::: {.hidden} $$ \def\RR{{\bf R}} \def\bold#1{{\bf #1}} \def\but{{\boldsymbol u_t}} \def\butp{{\boldsymbol u_{t+1}}} \def\beps{{\boldsymbol \varepsilon}} $$ ::: - Random walks * Simple random walk * Correlated random walk * Biased random walk * PDE - Point process models * Step-selection models ::: {.notes} Speaker notes go here. ::: # Random walks ## Simple random walk $$ {\boldsymbol u_{t+1}} = \but + \beps $$ where $$ {\boldsymbol \varepsilon} = \text{Norm}(0, \sigma^2 {\bf I}) $$ ## Simple random walk simulation {.smaller} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.cell code-block-bg='true'} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} sigma <- 0.05 T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) for(t in 2:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + epsilon ## Equivalent to two lines above ## u[t,] <- rnorm(n=2, mean=u[t-1,], sd=0.05) } ``` :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} plot(u, asp=1, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), xlab="", ylab="") arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="54%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-rw-simple-1.png){fig-align="top" width="100%"} ::: :::: ## Biased random walk \begin{equation} {\boldsymbol u_{t+1}} = \but + {\bf B}(\but-{\boldsymbol s}) + \beps \label{eq:brwalk} \end{equation} where, typically $$ \begin{equation} {\bf B} = \begin{pmatrix} \rho & 0 \\ 0 & \rho \end{pmatrix} \end{equation} $$ with $\rho \in [0,1]$ ## Biased random walk simulation :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} sigma <- 0.05 rho <- 0.1 # Bias towards activity center T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) s <- c(0.5,0.5) B <- diag(rho,2) for(t in 2:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + B%*%(s-u[t-1,]) + epsilon } ``` :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} plot(u, asp=1, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), xlab="", ylab="") points(s[1], s[2], pch=16, col=rgb(0,0,1,0.5), cex=2.5) arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="54%"} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-brw-simple-1.png){width="100%"} ::: :::: ## Correlated random walk \begin{equation} \butp = \but + {\bf R}(\but-{\boldsymbol u}_{t-1}) + \beps \label{eq:crwalk} \end{equation} where $$ {\bf R} = \gamma \begin{pmatrix} \cos(\theta) & -\sin(\theta) \\ \sin(\theta) & \cos(\theta) \end{pmatrix} $$ with $\theta \in [-\pi,\pi]$ being the expected turn angle, and $\gamma \in [0,1]$ dampening the persistence. ## Correlated random walk simulation ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code style="font-size: 0.85em;"} sigma <- 0.05 gamma <- 0.8 ## Damping of correlated walk theta <- 0 ## Correlation (-pi,pi) T <- 50 u <- matrix(NA, nrow=T, ncol=2) u[1,] <- c(0.5,0.5) u[2,] <- rnorm(2, u[1,], sd=0.05) R <- gamma*matrix(c(cos(theta),sin(theta),-sin(theta),cos(theta)), nrow=2, ncol=2) for(t in 3:T) { epsilon <- rnorm(n=2, mean=c(0,0), sd=sigma) u[t,] <- u[t-1,] + R%*%(u[t-1,]-u[t-2,]) + epsilon } par(mai=c(0.7,0.7,0.1,0.1)) plot(u, asp=1, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1), xlab="", ylab="") arrows(u[1:49,1], u[1:49,2], u[2:50,1], u[2:50,2], length=0.1, col="blue") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-movement_files/figure-revealjs/fig-crw-simple-1.png){#fig-crw-simple width=672} ::: ::: ## Random walks along environmental gradients $$ \butp = \but + {\bf D}\nabla x(\but) + \beps $$ where $\bf D = \alpha {\bf I}$ is a $2\times2$ matrix describing the effect of the gradient in the environment ($\nabla x$) at location $\but$. Positive values of $\alpha$ describe the scenario in which the organism tends to move in the direction of the gradient. If $\alpha=0$, the individual will ignore the environment as it follows a simple random walk. ## Environment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(430) library(terra) delta <- 0.025 ## Resolution grid0 <- seq(delta/2, 1-delta/2, delta) grid <- cbind(rep(grid0, each=length(grid0)), rep(grid0, times=length(grid0))) distmat <- as.matrix(dist(grid)) ## Distance b/w grid points npixels <- nrow(distmat) V <- exp(-0.1*distmat) ## Covariance R <- chol(V) X <- t(R) %*% rnorm(npixels) ## Gaussian random field Xr <- rast(cbind(grid, X), type="xyz", ## Convert to raster crs="+proj=utm +zone=17 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs +type=crs") terr <- terrain(Xr, v=c("slope","aspect")) ## Slope and aspect vfieldU <- terr$slope * sin(terr$aspect) ## x-coord of arrow head vfieldV <- terr$slope * cos(terr$aspect) ## y-coord of arrow head vfieldData <- cbind(as.data.frame(Xr, xy=TRUE), v1=values(vfieldU), v2=values(vfieldV)) names(vfieldData) <- c("s1","s2","X","v1","v2") ``` ::: ## Simulating random walks along environmental gradients # Point process models

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
